name: Private menu operation-gate runtime capability exposure
phase: Discovery and specification only; implementation requires separate explicit authorization
architecturalPurpose: Expose the existing menu service, workspace and authorization-before-continuation gate through additive trusted runtime factories backed by one concrete service, preserving existing narrow factory contracts without creating transport or activating infrastructure.

currentContracts.H: createPrivateFoodMenuRuntimeComposition(input: FoodPrivateMenuRuntimeCompositionInput): FoodPrivateMenuRuntimeCapabilities returns exactly frozen { service, workspace }; service: FoodPrivateMenuService and workspace: FoodPrivateMenuWorkspaceController.
currentContracts.J: createPrivateFoodMenuRuntimeFromServerContext(input: FoodPrivateMenuServerContextInput): FoodPrivateMenuServerContextResult returns frozen { ok: true, value: exactHBundle } or fixed configuration-unavailable. Its success type refers to FoodPrivateMenuRuntimeCapabilities, not a duplicated structural bundle.
currentContracts.K: SingleAdminFoodMenuService implements both FoodPrivateMenuService and FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate. runAuthorized<T>(callback: () => T | Promise<T>): Promise<FoodMenuAuthorizedCallbackResult<T>> is separate from the unchanged 23-operation FoodPrivateMenuService type.
currentContracts.I: acquirePrivateFoodMenuDatabaseFromEnvironment validates environment plus injected bindingName and returns only FoodD1Database or fixed configuration failure; it neither constructs nor returns menu runtime capabilities.
currentContracts.staticVisibility: FoodPrivateMenuService has no runAuthorized member. Neither current H nor J declares a gate field, so future transport cannot obtain FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate through their static contracts without an unsafe cast/probe/concrete implementation dependency.
currentContracts.compatibilityEvidence: H/J specs and tests explicitly require exactly service/workspace keys. Adding a mandatory operationGate to the existing interface/output would alter those contracts and typed fakes, even though consumers merely destructuring the two old properties could still work. FOOD-002K already calls for preserving existing narrow runtime factories.

selectedArchitecture.decision: Add companion H and J factories with a new extended capability type; keep existing two-field factories and types intact. Construct one concrete service and expose two narrow interface views of it, plus the existing workspace. No I change is required.
selectedArchitecture.namingRationale: FOOD-001K uses gate for a distinct capability. Use operationGate in the new menu bundle to identify FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate explicitly, as proposed by this direction; do not add a second alias named gate.
selectedArchitecture.capabilityDefinition: export interface FoodPrivateMenuOperationRuntimeCapabilities extends FoodPrivateMenuRuntimeCapabilities { readonly operationGate: FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate; }
selectedArchitecture.bundle: Object.freeze({ service, workspace, operationGate: service }) with service statically known as SingleAdminFoodMenuService during construction, and workspace constructed from that exact instance.
selectedArchitecture.serverResultDefinition: export type FoodPrivateMenuOperationServerContextResult = Readonly<{ ok: true; value: FoodPrivateMenuOperationRuntimeCapabilities } | { ok: false; error: Readonly<{ code: 'configuration-unavailable'; message: 'Food menu database configuration is unavailable.' }> }>;
selectedArchitecture.newInputs: None. Reuse the exact existing H and J input types. No new binding name, administrator, resolver, expectedOrigin or request input.
rejectedAlternatives: No-change conclusion is invalid because the declared static contracts hide the gate.
Do not widen FoodPrivateMenuService or add runAuthorized to the workspace.
Do not alter the old bundle shape or require existing consumers/fakes to provide a gate.
Do not cast/downcast narrow service into a gate, use instanceof or probe runAuthorized to obtain it, construct a second service, or configure a second authorization policy.

sameInstanceRequirements: Exactly one D1FoodMenuRepository, one SingleAdminFoodMenuService and one workspace per successful companion composition call; workspace captures that concrete service.

operationGate === concreteService and service === concreteService are required where the concrete local type is known. Object.is(capabilities.service, capabilities.operationGate) must be true; these are two interface views of one object, not a forwarding wrapper or clone.

Public narrow service and gate types have disjoint method sets; direct service === operationGate expressions may trigger TypeScript's no-overlap comparison diagnostic. Use Object.is in consumer tests without casting or widening either exported interface.
Do not invoke both old and companion factories to assemble one result. Each invocation produces one fresh graph; separate calls intentionally yield independent graphs.

J companion creates exactly one fresh AstroPrincipalSessionStore, D1PrincipalRepository and DefaultSessionPrincipalResolver, then invokes the H companion exactly once. No duplicated resolver, repository, administrator input or policy.
requiredHChanges: Add a type-only FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate import, the new extended capability interface and companion factory in private-menu-runtime-composition.ts.

A private construction helper may share existing input capture/validation and one repository/service/workspace construction between old and companion factories. It must retain the concrete service type internally so gate assignment is checked statically without capability casts.

Preserve capture order database/readDependencies/callerResolver/administratorPrincipalId, exact injected references, receiver behavior, constructor order and existing fixed TypeErrors. Old factory returns exactly frozen service/workspace; companion includes operationGate before freezing.

No success/failure envelope or promise is added to H. Preserve outer-input, repository, service and workspace constructor error handling unchanged; structural failure creates no partial output or fallback graph.
requiredJChanges: Add companion factory and result type in private-menu-server-adapter.ts, importing the H companion and new capability type. Existing J function/input/result remain intact.

Share existing structural validation, single property capture, I acquisition and request-scoped identity construction in a private helper if needed. Do not change validation ordering, administrator parsing, optional now behavior, exact environment/binding/read references or failure handling.
Old J delegates to old H and returns its exact two-field bundle. Companion J delegates to companion H and returns that exact three-field bundle in frozen success without reconstruction or cloning.

On I failure both return the exact I failure unchanged and construct no identity/H graph. Thrown dependency/identity/H construction remains fixed sanitized configuration-unavailable with existing message. No new error vocabulary or fallback.
No I source or typing change: its result is a database, not a bundle. Existing I callers and tests continue unchanged.
compatibility: Preserve FoodPrivateMenuRuntimeCapabilities, FoodPrivateMenuServerContextResult, both existing factory names/signatures and exact old output key sets. New extended capability is structurally usable where the old capability is accepted, but the old type does not claim a gate.

Keep all 23 FoodPrivateMenuService operations, FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate, FoodMenuAuthorizedCallbackResult, FoodPrivateMenuWorkspaceController and their semantics unchanged. No service/workspace/identity/persistence changes.
Existing narrow H/J tests remain valid, including exact shape, constructor instrumentation, fixed errors, purity and delegation. Add companion cases rather than weakening old assertions.
Earlier H no-gate exclusions remain true for its old factory. L permits only the distinct companion exposure; no transport, authorization redesign or widening of old APIs.

FOOD-001K precedent applies to separate narrow interfaces, same concrete instance, frozen bundle and companion APIs preserving old factories. Do not copy draft-specific acquisition keys, errors or controller exclusion; menu H already owns its workspace.
purityAndAuthorization: Both old and companion constructions remain synchronous, structural and I/O-free: zero session methods/clock calls, resolver calls, gate callbacks, authorization, database prepare/batch/statements, FOOD-001 reads, repository/service/workspace operations or request-body/network access.

Do not acquire globals, cloudflare:workers, request data, environment values beyond existing I/J validation, or production configuration. Structural assembly proves no session trust, live authorization, database/schema/migration readiness, primary consistency or menu activation.

Later operationGate.runAuthorized inherits K's fresh authorization, zero denied callbacks, exactly-once awaited opaque success and fixed callback-failed semantics. Every normal operation through service/workspace authorizes independently again, honoring revocation after gate success.
No authorization cache, token, inherited permission or authorization-once-per-request claim. Construction merely exposes existing capabilities, never executes them.
immutabilityAndExposure: Freeze the three-field companion capability bundle before returning it and freeze J result envelopes. Keep existing workspace frozen; do not deep-freeze service/repository/session/resolver/environment or injected dependencies.

service is typed only FoodPrivateMenuService, workspace only FoodPrivateMenuWorkspaceController and operationGate only FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate. Static narrow surfaces do not erase other methods on the shared concrete object; this is not a runtime facade or security sandbox claim.
Expose no repository/database/read dependencies/environment/session/principal repository/resolver/administrator/principal/token fields. Internal class private fields remain private.
Configuration failures remain separate from access errors, callback-failed, workspace feedback and repository outcomes. Do not reinterpret or merge them.
futureTransportPrerequisite: Transport may receive capabilities.operationGate and capabilities.workspace, or the narrow service if its later contract selects that surface. It need not know or instantiate the concrete service class.

Future flow: companion J runtime -> operationGate fresh authorization -> lazy continuation -> body read/parse -> normal workspace/service mutation -> another fresh E authorization. Denied gate means no body access.

Transport request schema/routing, policy checks, Origin/CSRF, body limits and feedback remain a separate discovery/specification slice. expectedOrigin and its trusted sourcing remain entirely outside L.
Implementation and validation of L's companion exposure are required before transport integrates through trusted runtime; specification alone does not make the gate available.

Companion H exposes exactly service/workspace/operationGate, shallow-frozen and not a promise; J companion returns exact H companion bundle in frozen success. Static gate consumption requires no casts or concrete class knowledge.

Instrument constructors/factory as existing H/J tests do: exactly one repository/service/workspace, workspace's service receiver same as gate/service, original read/database/admin/resolver arguments preserved. Object.is(service, operationGate) true.

Zero composition-time authorization/session/clock/database/FOOD-001/body operations for old and new paths. Repeated construction yields independent graphs with unchanged/unfrozen injected dependencies.
